purpose: Teach: 泙/蹐/癲/腓/磴/曚/儖/蕁

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 蓮さん、古典詩の水音、つまり泙の擬音研究を論文で扱いましたね
lines.en: Ren, you wrote your paper on classical poetry water sounds — the onomatopoeia of 泙, didn't you?
lines.style: Warm, measured acknowledgment. Gentle rise on his name. Curious but not testing. The tone of a teacher who's read the work and wants to hear him talk about it.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: はい、跼蹐、つまり蹐の語源と過度な遠慮の研究を論文で扱いました
lines.en: Yes, I wrote my paper on 跼蹐 — the etymology of 蹐 and the linguistics of excessive deference.
lines.style: Quiet, a touch uncertain. Correcting gently but clearly. Slight tension in the shoulders — he knows she got it slightly wrong, but he's respectful about the redirect.

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 蓮さん、癲癇、つまり癲発作の歴史的記録の研究を論文で扱いましたね
lines.en: Ren, your paper explored the historical records of 癲癇 — epilepsy, didn't it?
lines.style: Thoughtful, genuinely interested. Slower pace. She's not performing; she's checking in, seeing if he'll elaborate beyond the title.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: はい、下腿の腓腹筋、つまり腓の運動学を論文で扱いました
lines.en: Yes, I focused on the kinesiology of the calf muscle — the 腓腹筋, specifically the anatomy of 腓.
lines.style: Steady, more confident now. Not defensive, but clearer. He's finding his rhythm explaining something he knows well.

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 蓮さん、登山道の磴、つまり石段の地理研究を論文で扱いましたね
lines.en: Ren, I see you tackled mountain trails in your research — the geography of stone steps, the 磴.
lines.style: Gentle pause before speaking. Warm curiosity. She's drawing him out. The rhythm is slower, inviting him to fill the space.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: はい、曚気、つまり曚の薄暗さの古典詩研究を論文で扱いました
lines.en: Yes, I wrote on the twilight aesthetic in classical poetry — the 曚, that sense of dimness and obscurity.
lines.style: More animated now. He's settling into it. Slight energy lift on the explanation. Less hesitation, more presence.

lines.speaker: asuka_teacher
lines.jp: 蓮さん、古代の儖、つまり儖の人体表記の研究を論文で扱いましたね
lines.en: Ren, you also researched ancient notation systems, didn't you — how the 儖 character recorded the human form?
lines.style: Reflective, almost musing. She's drawing a line through his work, seeing the pattern. Genuine appreciation in her voice.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: はい、蕁麻疹、つまり蕁の皮膚反応の臨床研究を論文で扱いました
lines.en: Yes, my research traced the clinical manifestations of 蕁麻疹 — urticaria, the skin's immune response documented through 蕁.
lines.style: Clear, assured finish. He's found his footing. The 'yes' lands more solidly. He's no longer correcting so much as confidently sharing his expertise.
